name: klicktipp
description: KlickTipp toolkit: write, review and prepare KlickTipp email newsletters — drafts, block-by-block content, audience, sender, test sends and the dispatch confirmation — and read the opt-in processes of the account, over the KlickTipp MCP server.

interface.shortDescription: Write, review and prepare KlickTipp email newsletters block by block, and read the account's opt-in processes. The actual dispatch is always confirmed by a person in KlickTipp.
interface.longDescription: Connects to the KlickTipp MCP server (https://mcp.klicktipp.com/mcp, OAuth) and exposes two parts of the KlickTipp product API as tools. The newsletter itself: search newsletters, read one through projections for metadata, audience, delivery configuration and dispatch state, create and update a draft, configure sender and reply address, send a test to a verified address, and prepare the real dispatch. Its content: read the stored block document, show it rendered as a preview, put one of the account's own designs on it, and change it block by block — a tool per kind of block to add one, to rewrite its content, to restyle it, to move it or to take it out, each addressing a block by its uuid, so a change reaches exactly one block and the rest of the design stays as it is. A row can be bound to a display condition, so it reaches only the contacts that match it. Preparing the dispatch sends nothing: it validates everything, states who would receive the newsletter, and returns a short-lived single-use confirmation URL that only the logged-in person can open and confirm in KlickTipp. Opt-in: read the account's opt-in processes and their configuration, and resolve the pending or thank-you URL a subscriber is redirected to. Six skills ship with the plugin: `email` for the content of one email, `newsletter` for the hull around it, `splittest` for A/B tests, `crm` for the account's contact data, `dashboard` for reading an account's numbers as a dashboard, and `email-template-generator` for the plain business emails that are not newsletters. Each carries a reference of the tools it uses, with their pitfalls.
defaultPrompt: Show me my opt-in processes and which of them use double opt-in.
Create a newsletter draft for my webinar list, write it, and send a test to my own address.
Change the headline and the button text of my last newsletter, and leave the rest as it is.
